record.paper_title: Open problems of the 32nd Workshop on Cycles and Colourings
record.original_question: For every cubic bipartite graph G and every 3-list-assignment L of G, is it always possible to find three pairwise disjoint proper L-colorings?

evidence.quote: Hence, the following question arises: Is it possible to find three disjoint proper colourings in the case of cubic bipartite graphs?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a cubic bipartite graph, i.e., a 3-regular graph whose vertex set admits a bipartition into two independent sets. A list assignment $L$ on $G$ assigns to each vertex $v\in V$ a set $L(v)$ of colors; it is a 3-list-assignment if $|L(v)|=3$ for every $v\in V$. A proper $L$-coloring of $G$ is a function $c:V\to\bigcup_{v}L(v)$ such that $c(v)\in L(v)$ for every $v\in V$ and $c(u)\neq c(v)$ whenever $uv\in E$. Three proper $L$-colorings $c_1,c_2,c_3$ are called pairwise disjoint if $c_i(v)\neq c_j(v)$ for every $v\in V$ and every $1\le i<j\le 3$.

Prove or disprove: For every cubic bipartite graph $G$ and every 3-list-assignment $L$ on $G$, there exist three pairwise disjoint proper $L$-colorings of $G$ (equivalently, the list packing number of every cubic bipartite graph is at most 3).
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work on packing list-colorings (Cambie, Cames van Batenburg, Davies, Kang and others, 2023–2025) considers exactly this question for cubic graphs and notes that, while two disjoint proper L-colorings exist under girth assumptions, the existence of three pairwise disjoint L-colorings for every cubic bipartite graph with every 3-list assignment has not been established. The question is posed as an open problem in workshop problem collections and is not reported as resolved in the literature retrieved.

status_evidence.title: Packing list-colorings
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the list packing number, including bounds for bipartite graphs of the form min{Δ_A,Δ_B}+1, leaving open the cubic bipartite case at value 3.
status_evidence.claim: The list packing number of cubic bipartite graphs being at most 3 is not established in this work.

status_evidence.title: Disjoint list-colorings for planar graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Recent investigations into disjoint L-colorings; mentions cubic-graph cases as motivation but does not settle the cubic bipartite 3-list-packing question.
status_evidence.claim: The cubic bipartite case of 3-list-packing is not resolved in recent disjoint list-coloring literature.
